hypothesis: Adding exact named --project, --kind, --cursor and --snapshot-id options to CLI changes will expose the reviewed evidence views already available through core and MCP, including cross-project negative results, while preserving legacy positional compatibility, snapshot-bound pagination, read-only authority and fixed performance limits.

motivation.measuredBaselineGap: Core and MCP support project-only and kind-only change views. CLI positional syntax cannot express a kind-only view and treats named options as project identifiers.
motivation.acceptedUnintegrated: None. Every accepted entrypoint candidate through 0.9.0 is an ancestor of current main; vector/WASM/GNN work is deferred, not accepted.
motivation.forecast: Yesterday's should-act/should-abstain forecast makes cross-project negative-result retrieval a useful deterministic evidence view without adding decision automation. Today's separate forecast tests whether repeated-run reliability becomes a promotion requirement for future stateful MCP evaluation.

evaluator.authority: external read-only held-out runner; not shipped with the candidate

heldOut: named kind-only negative-result view matches an independent core oracle and contains only negative results
named project-only Ruflo view matches an independent core oracle and contains only Ruflo records
combined named filters equal legacy positional output and legacy behavior remains compatible
named filters compose with pagination and snapshot preconditions; changed filters or snapshot fail closed
missing, duplicate, unknown, control-character, authority-expanding and mixed named/positional forms fail nonzero with no JSON stdout
CLI and MCP expose identical snapshot, filters, ordering, results and continuation state; omitted named options preserve defaults

acceptance.heldOut: 6/6 and strictly better than the frozen 1/6 baseline
acceptance.tests: all existing and new tests pass on Node 22 and 24
acceptance.schemas: both marketplace schemas, four skills, six MCP tools and three resources validate
acceptance.metaharness: metaharness@0.4.16 retains 6/6 hard constraints; heuristic score alone is not proof
acceptance.security: zero confirmed high or critical findings; scanner coverage and residual risk disclosed

performance.design: 15 alternating pairs; 10000 filtered changes calls and 20 cold CLI starts per arm per pair; seed 1729
performance.changesP95: candidate no more than 20 percent and 0.05 ms above baseline median
performance.coldCliP95: candidate no more than 20 percent and 5 ms above baseline median
performance.rss: candidate no more than 5242880 bytes above baseline median

acceptance.package: normalized dependency closure unchanged, package validates and compressed archive remains below 40000 bytes

ruos.selection: Existing dedicated evolution-candidate desktop; the personal Mac and unrelated desktops are excluded.
ruos.evaluator: trusted Dream Machine main verifier at aa931caad5dd0108253645bba0ab1481ad7da0ee
ruos.preflight: This CLI-only candidate does not change desktop control, MCP UI, OAuth or a graphical user journey. A live desktop probe is not required for promotion. If attempted, require a current heartbeat before one harmless command and one screenshot.
ruos.decision: All candidate desktops have null last_heartbeat_at and peer telemetry is unavailable. Live desktop status is INCONCLUSIVE; do not issue an evidence-free probe or infer readiness from provisioning state.

memory.decision: Do not add RuVector, WASM or GNN complexity below the frozen record gate.

forecast.prediction: Agent-harness promotion reports will increasingly require independent repeated-run reliability, such as strict pass^k or a bounded flake rate, alongside single-run success for stateful MCP workflows.
forecast.criterion: At least two new primary benchmark implementations or reviewed production harnesses published after 2026-09-22 report fixed-workload results from at least four isolated independent runs per task and use all-runs success or a bounded-flake threshold as a promotion gate.

rollback: Revert the candidate commit; version 0.9.0 behavior remains its parent.
